issues.body: `_normalize_path_entry` still does not canonicalize internal `.` or `..` segments. GitHub Actions resolves `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` to the workspace-root divergence log, but `_glob_to_re` compares the unnormalized spelling to the root-relative target and returns false. The added traversal-shaped fixture contains `${{ matrix.shard }}`, so it is classified as unresolved dynamic input and returns true conservatively before dot-segment matching is exercised; it does not regress the static bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Lexically normalize static workspace-relative entries against a synthetic workspace root before glob matching, resolving `.` and `..` while preserving glob metacharacters; treat paths escaping the workspace conservatively. Add positive fixtures for `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` and `foo/./../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json`, a directory form normalizing to the workspace root, and an escaping-path case.
issues.title: Static dot-segment upload paths still bypass artifact detection

verdict.summary: Round 5 leaves the prior major finding unresolved. `_normalize_path_entry` still strips only leading `./` and trailing `/`; it does not lexically resolve internal `.` or `..` segments. The traversal-shaped fixture remains dynamic because it contains `${{ matrix.shard }}`, so `_upload_could_include` returns true conservatively before dot-segment matching is exercised. A static upload such as `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` resolves at runtime to the workspace-root divergence log but is still reported as unrelated. Progress is stagnant because the same major artifact-retention bypass remains at the same severity.
